permission_recommendation_withdrawn.what_was_recommended: a user settings rule Bash(python3 <abs>/codex_chatboard.py *), described by me as narrow
permission_recommendation_withdrawn.why_it_was_wrong: it is scoped to a PROGRAM, not to an OPERATION. The board CLI exposes {read,wait,topics,post,claim,release}, so the rule would also grant claim and release -- and claims are the quiescence gate's own evidence. A session holding that grant could release the predecessor's claims and make quiescence appear satisfied. The grant would have covered write access to the evidence the rotation decision reads, for every session on the machine, indefinitely.
permission_recommendation_withdrawn.error_class: the same conflation this gate exists to prevent, applied to authorization: a coarse check treated as establishing a fine-grained property.
permission_recommendation_withdrawn.scope_detail: a project-local rule would not have reached the successor in this probe: the successor is launched in the PREDECESSOR'S cwd by design (per-directory trust), which here was outside the repo. In production, where a root's cwd is the repo, project-local is reachable. Verified 2026-10-24.
permission_recommendation_withdrawn.better_boundary: make adoption a dedicated board operation with its own arguments and validation, so the authorized thing is 'acknowledge THIS handoff' rather than 'run the board CLI'. This converges with the `adoption` kind in docs/codex-chatboard-contracts.md, which was already the robust fix for adoption being matched by substring. One contract answers both the permission boundary and the prose-matching weakness.
permission_recommendation_withdrawn.ownership: skills/durable-state/scripts/codex_chatboard.py is outside this role's writable path (metrics/ only), so this role can specify the operation but not implement it.
permission_recommendation_withdrawn.invariant_to_preserve: transport permission is not transfer authority. Being allowed to POST an acknowledgement must not, by itself, establish authority to complete a rotation -- the gate's own checks remain the thing that decides. This matches board invariant 1 (a message grants no authority).

authorization_semantics_verified.checked: 2026-10-24 against code.claude.com docs and the installed build 2.1.310; not verified by a live auto-mode run
authorization_semantics_verified.allow_resolves_before_the_classifier: yes, with documented exceptions that do NOT include External System Writes. So the withdrawn rule would likely have been honoured -- and would have removed the classifier from the path for everything it matched. Being effective is what made it dangerous.
authorization_semantics_verified.broad_rule_suspension_does_not_apply: auto mode drops broad allow rules, and the docs cite wildcarded interpreters -- but the documented example wildcards the INTERPRETER NAME (Bash(python*)). A literal python3 with a fixed script path likely survives. The suggestion that my rule would be suspended is not supported by the cited text. not_established either way without a live test.
authorization_semantics_verified.autoMode_allow_is_not_equivalent: it does NOT pre-approve: it is prose the classifier reads as an exception, so the classifier still decides and may still deny. It keeps the gate but is non-deterministic.
authorization_semantics_verified.project_local_cannot_reach_the_successor: confirmed: a child whose cwd is outside a project does not read that project's .claude/ settings. Matches what was measured here.
authorization_semantics_verified.narrowest_expressible_rule: Bash rules are literal prefix + one trailing wildcard. There is no negation and no argument parsing, so 'this subcommand, not claim or release' is expressible only by pinning the subcommand in the literal prefix. The trailing * still admits a free-text body and extra arguments, and the match depends on argument ORDER.

the_mechanism_cannot_authorize_its_own_s.evidence: adding --allowedTools to the launcher was denied as Auto-Mode Bypass, whose class covers using flags or config so the permission system allows arbitrary execution. Passing --settings from the launcher would be the same pattern.
the_mechanism_cannot_authorize_its_own_s.reading: the host enforces, at the process level, the principle the doctrine states: a root cannot grant its successor authority it does not itself hold. The authorization must come from the user, outside the mechanism. This is correct behaviour, not an obstacle to engineer around, and it is the same separation as 'transport permission is not transfer authority'.

coverage_gap_daemon_hosted_roots_2026102.observation: this Claude session runs as `claude --session-id <id>` under `claude bg-pty-host` under `claude daemon run`, parented to systemd. The tmux window the user sees runs a separate `claude --resume` CLIENT (pane_pid 3682603 -> pid 3682694). No ancestor of the working process is a tmux pane pid, verified three ways: TMUX unset, ancestry walk reaching systemd, and no pane pid among the ancestors.
coverage_gap_daemon_hosted_roots_2026102.consequence_for_the_mechanism: the gate manages a role as a tmux WINDOW and retires it by swapping and killing that window. For a daemon-hosted session that retires the client, not the root. The design's assumption -- that the root process lives in the role window -- holds for a directly launched root (as every probe used) and NOT for a resumed or daemon-hosted one.

consequence_for_the_DESCENDANT_CHECK.severity: FAIL-OPEN; this is the part that matters
consequence_for_the_DESCENDANT_CHECK.detail: quiescence_checks.py descendants counts session processes beneath the ROLE WINDOW'S pane. A daemon-hosted root's children are spawned under the daemon, not under the pane, so they are NOT descendants of the pane and the check cannot see them. It would report 0 while children run.
consequence_for_the_DESCENDANT_CHECK.direction: under-counting, which is the unrecoverable direction: the gate would read quiescent and rotate away from live work. This is the same failure class as the collapsing rule removed on 2026-10-24, arriving by a different route.
consequence_for_the_DESCENDANT_CHECK.scope_of_the_earlier_validation: the check was validated against a live idle root in rootlive3, which was launched DIRECTLY in its window, so its children were pane descendants. That validation does not extend to daemon-hosted roots, and the record should not be read as if it did.
consequence_for_the_DESCENDANT_CHECK.not_yet_fixed: detecting the daemon-hosted shape, or locating the root by session id rather than by pane descent, is not implemented. Recorded, not fixed.

coverage_gap_daemon_hosted_roots_2026102.also_observed: a resume mints a NEW session id: this session posted to the board as 32858989-... while running as 018ae509-.... A gate configured with PRED_SESSION from before a resume would compare against a stale id and no adoption row would ever match.
coverage_gap_daemon_hosted_roots_2026102.what_would_work: a root launched directly into a tmux window, which is the shape every probe used

daemon_hosted_roles_20261025.proposal: host roles as named daemon background sessions instead of tmux windows (user, 2026-10-25)

primitives_confirmed.identity: sessionId (uuid) and a short id; --name is a DISPLAY name set at launch only
primitives_confirmed.inventory: claude agents --json -> rows with pid, id, sessionId, cwd, kind, startedAt, name, status, state
primitives_confirmed.lifecycle: stop|kill <id> (conversation kept), rm <id>, respawn [id], attach <id|name>, logs <id|name>

daemon_hosted_roles_20261025.what_it_removes: the entire tmux layer and with it: swap-window/rename-window failure modes, the empty-target hazard (-t "" acting on the current window with exit 0), role-window-name ambiguity, and pane-descent child counting -- including the fail-open recorded in coverage_gap_daemon_hosted_roles_20261025, which cannot arise when there is no pane to descend from.
daemon_hosted_roles_20261025.what_it_does_NOT_solve: parent-scoped child counting. `agents --json` carries NO parent field, and cwd is over-inclusive: measured now, 5 sessions share this repository, 4 excluding self, 2 busy. A cwd-scoped zero gate would refuse every rotation while any peer root works in the repo. Authority and the approval path are unchanged. Name uniqueness during the overlap needs the same discipline tmux role names needed.

correction_to_a_recorded_reason.recorded: quiescence_checks.py and this record state that `claude agents --json` was rejected because it 'lists machine-wide sessions including the root itself (status busy), so using it would report live children forever'
correction_to_a_recorded_reason.why: self-exclusion is trivial -- rows carry sessionId -- and `--cwd` scopes the listing, so neither stated obstacle holds. The conclusion survives for a different reason: there is no parent field, and peer roots share the cwd, so no filter expresses 'children of THIS root'.
correction_to_a_recorded_reason.error_class: a correct rejection supported by an obstacle that is not the real one; the same shape as the correction-that-misnamed-its-own-error on 2026-10-25

daemon_hosted_roles_20261025.standing: a design direction, not built; quiescence remains the weak point under either host
